decisions: All controls not expressly printed above are reconstruction assumptions, including nominal hex envelopes and washer sections. Smooth thread envelopes represent connections without a helical thread claim.

MX101 port and MX100 starboard are separate handed rail/web brackets. Their exact casting sections and adjustment mechanism are not resolved in HB15; the selected frame is an explicit inferred load path between documented attachments.
MX98 axes point forward from M264. Estimated integral blind bosses extend inward from its existing X220 front face. Do not replace or relocate existing MX25 receivers.

MX99 is represented as a vertical stepped stud: half-inch lower body,3/8-inch upper end. MX102 locks the lower attachment; the half-inch nut and one small washer support the bracket; the second small washer and3/8-inch nut clamp it. This interprets the exact catalogue hardware, not a proven historical arrangement.
Two integral M250 bosses provide blind receivers without opening the bearing cavity. Preserve the grease passage and existing gland/cover interfaces.

The earlier pump core position[300,0,210] was only a clearance study. The belt plane at coreX396 would pass through the housing. This candidate moves the pump toX420, placing its pulley atX516 beyond the X490 input coupling.

Pump height is derived from an open-belt length using assumed pitch radii89.25/108.3mm. The latter corresponds to an estimated228.6mm drive pulley OD with6mm radial deduction, broadly proportional to HB71 against its printed2-inch shaft. Neither diameter nor belt pitch convention is independently established. The physical belt/drive pulley is deferred to clutch construction.
Both pitch radii varied together by+/-6mm represent three length-reference scenarios, not exhaustive uncertainty bounds. Height must change with the eventual clutch/belt evidence.

Pump foot holes move fromY+/-87 to+/-90.5mm and ledges widen4mm so the printed3/8-inch bolt heads clear the adjacent casting wall. Original core remains preserved; only its installed base definition is revised.

Split washers are modeled in the compressed static state with an open split. Original free-state helicity and spring stiffness are unverified. Do not count mounting-set identities as extra physical solids.
